registry.title: int8-quantized GEMM (Vulkan) vs f16 tensor-core GEMM (CUDA)
registry.applies_to: vulkan vs cuda, prefill GEMM on quantized weight types
registry.mechanism: Vulkan takes the int8 MMQ path for types its policy allows (src/vulkan/mod.rs:819); sm_70 CUDA always takes the f16 path because `i8_gemm` is false on Volta (src/cuda/mod.rs:558). X is quantized to int8 per 32 elements on one side and rounded to f16 on the other, so the two GEMMs multiply different numbers.
registry.arm: STRATA_MMQ= forces the f16 GEMM on Vulkan and isolates this entry

registry.title: f16 conversion rounding vs truncation
registry.applies_to: cuda vs vulkan, f16 GEMM operands
registry.mechanism: CUDA converts operands with `__float2half` (round to nearest even); this driver's SPIR-V `OpFConvert` truncates toward zero, so the two f16 GEMMs see different operands.
registry.measured: 5.41e-4 (IQ2_XS), 4.79e-5 (F32) relative L2 per-op (docs/V100-results.md:303-310); recorded, not asserted, by tests/kernels.rs:409

registry.title: summation order (mma.sync tile order vs cooperative matrices vs FMA)
registry.applies_to: cuda vs vulkan and tensor-core vs FMA, same f16 products
registry.mechanism: sm_70 CUDA sums the f16 products through `mma.sync.m8n8k4` (src/cuda/kernels.cu:mma884); Vulkan has no VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix on this driver and sums through its own workgroup reduction (src/vulkan/shaders/gemmi.glsl), the FMA arms sum serially. The products are the same, the accumulation tree is not.
registry.measured: 2.6e-7 .. 8.2e-7 relative L2 per backend against its own reference; 1e-6 .. 1e-4 cross-backend on the same math (docs/V100-results.md:303-310)
registry.arm: STRATA_VK_NO_COOP= forces Vulkan off cooperative matrices; STRATA_GEMM_FMA=1 the CUDA FMA path

registry.title: no cooperative matrices on Vulkan (V100 driver)
registry.mechanism: Vulkan 1.4.312 on this host exposes no VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix, so Vulkan cannot use the same MMA instruction shape as CUDA; its prefill GEMM and attention use explicit workgroup reductions. This is the Vulkan side of `summation-order`.
registry.measured: 1e-6 .. 5e-4 relative L2 where only the reduction tree differs (docs/V100-results.md:529-551)

registry.title: q8 KV cache quantization
registry.applies_to: `--kv q8` arms only (not used by --llama-numerics parity)
registry.mechanism: `--kv q8` stores K/V as int8 with per-32 scales, the default path stores f16; the attention scores read quantized K and the output quantized V. `--kv q8` does not combine with `--llama-numerics` by design (src/main.rs), so parity keeps f16 KV.
registry.measured: 1.55e-3 .. 2.06e-3 relative L2 q8 vs f16 decode/prefill (docs/V100-results.md:556-558); KV bytes 341/642 = 53.1 % (M2-T6)

registry.title: expert-slot layout and MoE routing order
registry.mechanism: The router's top-k expert ids are the same, but the per-slot gather order and the combine reduction order differ between the CUDA and Vulkan MoE kernels; parity runs also pass `--fixed-experts` so routing is identical on both sides.
registry.measured: not measured above the summation-order floor in the M1/M0 per-op runs; re-recorded in the M2-T7 window

registry.title: llama.cpp's own two modes disagree at this position
registry.mechanism: llama.cpp run as one batch and llama.cpp run token-by-token disagree at this position (target/llama-batch-argmax.json, tools/selfparity.py); the two engines sit on either side of a near-tie whose winner depends on summation order. The v1 gate counts a token that matches either llama.cpp mode.
